"For example, pets offer benefits like automatic looting of corpses..."

That's a convenience item, not P2W.

I generally agree with this - what actually worries me is that you can sell these premium items for in-game cash, which could have devastating effects on the games economy. Maybe I'm just paranoid, but ever since Blizzard pulled the bullshit with the Diablo 3 auction house, I'm a bit sensible on these topics.

Plus, the EU/US version is not F2P like the Asian version, which always had a cash shop with these kind of items (the EU/US one was limited to purely cosmetical items, IIRC). You might argue that, unless the developer pushes new expansions as was the case with Guild Wars, the developer is not only in its good right but actually has to sell these items to keep the servers running, but it still may leave a bitter aftertaste to know that you paid a few dozen bucks for what the Asians effectively got for free.

And, last but not least, banning people on your forums for voicing criticism (and assuming that said criticism is not just rampant shitposting) rarely is a good idea.
As for selling the item in game - WoW has a token you can buy for real money and then sell on the auction house for in-game gold, and GW2 has a similar process via the Gem Store.

I must admit that I never really played GW myself. As for WoW - I played that until mid-Cataclysm, and I remember there was a shitstorm of epic proportions when they opened the in-game shop (and mind you, back then it only had cosmetic items and pets). That World of Warcraft also runs on a monthly subscription rather than being a buy-to-play title did not at all help in this situation, and WoW's user numbers have been decreasing more or less continously since Cataclysm, if memory serves.

At any rate - so long as we are not talking expansions, excluding game content from users that have actually paid for the game is not okay in my book. Games that used to be P2W and then went F2P may be a special case, although I would argue that, in such scenarios, the users who actually paid for the game before it became F2P should have some kind of premium membership by default - a notable exception perhaps lying in cosmetic items, as per Team Fortress 2.
